column2: Match the approved D.N.A. paint-overs in Card Game Art / Paintovers (PAINTOVER-DNA-HUB, -CUBICLE-FIELDS, -THE-QUEUE, -RECORDS-BASEMENT, -EXECUTIVE-APPROACH) and the quality of PAINTOVER-TOWN.png. D.N.A. look: bureaucratic, gloomy, deadpan funny; perpetual 4:59 PM overcast, cold flat light with sickly green ghost glows. Palette: gray #6E7470, sage #9BB59A, dark slate #3D4A44, parchment #C9C6B8, ghost green #4FBF7A, red-tape red #8A2E2E. Gray stone office blocks, filing-cabinet towers, queue barriers, columned civic halls. Painted, not pixel: clean bold shapes, soft cel-shaded painting. No text or letters anywhere.
Seamless, tileable, hand-painted texture viewed perfectly straight-on (orthographic). Flat, even, neutral lighting. Evenly distributed detail; edges match so it tiles. Square 1024x1024.

A single hand-painted object or detail, viewed straight-on (or from the low game camera for props), centered, fully transparent background (PNG). Soft painted shading, no cast shadow outside the object, crisp edges. Slightly oversized storybook proportions.

6 related items on ONE transparent image in a 3x2 grid, each centered in its cell with wide clear empty gaps (nothing touching), same scale and lighting, viewed straight-on. Claude slices them apart. 2048x1365 (or 1536x1024).

A single hand-painted plant seen from a low camera slightly above (about 25 degrees down), storybook shapes, base at the bottom center, fully transparent background, no ground or cast shadow. 1024x1536.

Concept: the landmark alone in a three-quarter view from the low game camera, plain flat light background, clear silhouette, a 1.7 m person beside it for scale. Backdrop: a wide distant-scenery layer along the bottom with a transparent sky above, atmospheric haze; left and right edges match if noted.

Save to Card Game Art / Pending Review; approved files go to Card Game Art / Approved_ZoneKits / DNA. Reused from earlier batches (don't remake): TEX-DNA-CARPET, -MARBLE, -LINOLEUM, -CHECKERTILE, -PANELING, -WALLPAPER, DEC-PAPERS, DEC-ECTOPLASM, and the shared ENV-* kit.
